A free, open course for pathology residents. No coding experience needed.


You will train your first deep learning model on histology in **lesson 1**, before learning any code.
Each later lesson opens one of the boxes you used without explanation, until you can run a project of your own
on your department's slides and present it at a congress.

The course is inspired by fast.ai's [Practical Deep Learning for Coders](https://course.fast.ai):
**whole game first, code before theory, and notebooks as the textbook.**

## Who it is for

- Pathology residents (and pathologists) with **no coding background**
- About **4 to 6 hours a week**: roughly two weeks per lesson for lessons 1 to 10, then a few months for the capstone
- Everything runs in your web browser on free cloud GPUs. You do not need to install anything.

## How it works

1. Read a lesson here, or open it directly on **Kaggle** (recommended) or **Google Colab** with the badges at the top of each lesson.
2. Run the notebook cell by cell. Explanations sit between the code.
3. Do the homework: *now do it on your own data*.
4. Share your notebook publicly. Over the course it becomes your portfolio.
5. Check yourself against the lesson's **checkpoint**. Lessons 5, 9 and 11 are formal checkpoints assessed by a supervisor:
   you move on when you are ready, not when the calendar says so.

New here? Start with [Getting started](getting-started.qmd).

::: {.callout-note}
An independent, volunteer project of the Marmara Pathology Community, an informal group. It is not an official course of any university, hospital or other institution, and is not endorsed by one. For education only, not for use on patients. See [About](about.qmd).
:::

## Lessons

| # | Lesson | What you will do |
|---|--------|------------------|
| 1 | [Your first model](lessons/01-first-model/lesson.ipynb) | Train a tumor versus normal patch classifier on PatchCamelyon, without writing code |
| 2 | [Inside a digital slide](lessons/02-inside-a-slide/lesson.ipynb) 🚧 | Whole slide images, scanners, formats; annotation and a pixel classifier in QuPath |
| 3 | [Just enough Python](lessons/03-just-enough-python/lesson.ipynb) 🚧 | Read lesson 1's notebook line by line |
| 4 | [Tiling a slide](lessons/04-tiling-a-slide/lesson.ipynb) 🚧 | OpenSlide, tissue masks, patch extraction |
| 5 | [Data done right](lessons/05-data-done-right/lesson.ipynb) 🚧 | Patient-level splits, leakage, metrics. ✅ **Checkpoint** |
| 6 | [Stain variation and augmentation](lessons/06-stain-and-augmentation/lesson.ipynb) 🚧 | Stain normalisation and augmentation |
| 7 | [Segmentation](lessons/07-segmentation/lesson.ipynb) 🚧 | Glands and nuclei with U-Net; Dice and IoU |
| 8 | [Foundation models](lessons/08-foundation-models/lesson.ipynb) 🚧 | Feature extraction with UNI, CONCH or similar |
| 9 | [Slide-level prediction](lessons/09-slide-level-prediction/lesson.ipynb) 🚧 | Multiple instance learning for Gleason/ISUP grading on PANDA. ✅ **Checkpoint** |
| 10 | [Trust](lessons/10-trust/lesson.ipynb) 🚧 | Validation, bias, explainability, regulation, data governance |
| 11 | [Capstone](lessons/11-capstone/lesson.ipynb) 🚧 | Your own project on anonymized departmental slides, ending in a congress abstract. ✅ **Final checkpoint** |

🚧 = under construction.
